items.title: Eric Brown Interview, 1969-10-26
items.q: Bill Tope, banjo. ... This was recorded in February of 1955, and is Warwick Dyer's last tune.

ctx.x: The End The End The End The End The End The End The End The End The End The End That one was called the original slow drag, and that's an original composition by Frank Johnson. It was recorded December 6th, 1949. Issued on Swaggy JCS 33768.

The real character of this band was Warwick Dyer, the trombone player, and around him revolved a lot of the jazz of this time, and he was unfortunately killed in a car accident. And the bottom more or less dropped out of jazz at that particular time, not only because he was killed, but because of the usual things like rock and roll and television started around about that time. Anyway, Warwick drank quite a bit, so... Sorry. Warwick drank quite a bit, so Frank Johnson composed a tune called Waka the Fish. Through…

Now we're going to listen to Waka the Fish, Frank Johnson's band.
